Decision: split into five children; the parent keeps only the assembly (supplied step 1, the transfer from c to Df in step 4, and step 6).

Why split. The supplied proof bundles four obligations of different kinds. None is available in Mathlib, in SimonGMT, or as an accepted DAG declaration with a matching type:
(a) the varifold-to-parameter transfer of step 2 (book (10)-(11)): campanato_from_tilt;
(b) the Lebesgue-point identification of step 3: campanato_ae_center;
(c) the midpoint-averaging Hoelder estimate of step 4 for the Campanato centres c(z) = p_{S(F z)}: campanato_center_holder. The printed computation never uses that x_1, x_2 are Lebesgue points, so it is stated for all pairs in B^o_{R/16}(0);
(d) the C^1 criterion of step 5, split into two parts:
 - lipschitz_ae_derivative: a continuous a.e.-derivative of a Lipschitz map is its derivative everywhere (Fubini along segments, FTC for absolutely continuous functions, density);
 - c1_holder_extension: a Hoelder bound on a full-measure set gives a continuous extension, so f is C^1 with the same bound (depends on lipschitz_ae_derivative).
The accepted any_radius_campanato assumes that g is continuous, which is what (d) has to prove, so it cannot replace these children.

- campanato_from_tilt takes the graph-comparison inequality as hypothesis (vi) and the a.e. strong measurability of V.tangentProj as hypothesis (v), with exactly the types of those siblings' conclusions;
- the analytic children prove their Hilbert-Schmidt facts internally;
- the integrability bound in child 1 uses operator norms (4(n+l)), so it needs no rank information.

subproblems.title: Tilt-excess decay on spt V gives a parameter-domain Campanato bound for the graph tangent projections (book 5.2 (10)-(11))
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0, U a subset of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the contract (carrier M contained in U, multiplicity theta, theta H^n-integrable on M cap K for each compact K contained in U), mu := V.weight and p_w := V.tangentProj w. Let q be a linear isometry of R^(n+l), f : R^n -> R^l, S : R^(n+l) -> subspaces of R^(n+l), R > 0 and A, e arbitrary reals. Write F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)), Df(x) := fderiv f x and G(x) := the orthogonal projection (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto (span{graphPoint v (Df(x) v) : v in R^n}).map q. Assume: (i) the closed ball B_R(0) of R^(n+l) is contained in U; (ii) f(0) = 0; (iii) f is 1-Lipschitz on the closed ball B^n_R(0); (iv) spt V cap B_R(0) = q(graphOver f (B^n_R(0))) cap B_R(0); (v) w -> p_w is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (vi) for every Phi : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l)) -> [0, infinity] with (w, P) -> Phi w P measurable and every measurable D contained in the open ball B^o_{R/2}(0) of R^n: lintegral_D Phi(F(x), G(x)) dx <= lintegral_{q(graphOver f D)} Phi(y, p_y) dmu(y); (vii) V.tiltExcess zeta s (S zeta) <= A (s/R)^e for every zeta in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0) and every 0 < s <= R/2. Then for every z in the closed ball B^n_{R/4}(0) and every 0 < s <= R/4: lintegral over the closed ball B^n_{s/2}(z) of ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - (S(F(z))).starProjection)) dx <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^e).

Source: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 5.2, (10)-(11)), with the graph-comparison inequality (sibling allard52_graph_comparison of the parent) and the a.e. measurability of the tangent map (sibling allard52_tangent_ae of the parent) taken as the explicit hypotheses (vi) and (v). The integrability bound uses the operator norm (|p_w - P|^2 <= 4(n+l)) instead of the rank, so no dimension information about S is needed.

Hypotheses (as in the statement): (i) the closed ball B_R(0) of R^(n+l) is contained in U; (ii) f(0) = 0; (iii) f is 1-Lipschitz on the closed ball B^n_R(0); (iv) spt V cap B_R(0) = q(graphOver f (B^n_R(0))) cap B_R(0); (v) w -> V.tangentProj w is V.weight-a.e. strongly measurable; (vi) for every Phi : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l)) -> [0, infinity] with uncurry Phi measurable and every measurable D contained in the open ball B^o_{R/2}(0) of R^n, integral^-_D Phi(F(x), G(x)) dx <= integral^-_{q(graphOver f D)} Phi(y, p_y) dmu(y); (vii) V.tiltExcess zeta s (S zeta) <= A (s/R)^e for all zeta in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0) and 0 < s <= R/2. Here R > 0 and A, e are arbitrary reals.

Notation. mu := V.weight, p_w := V.tangentProj w, F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)), Df(x) := fderiv f x, G(x) := starProjection of (span{graphPoint v (Df(x) v)}).map q, hsNormSq(T) := sum_i ||T e_i||^2 (e_i the standard basis vectors of the domain), ||.|| the Euclidean/operator norm. All balls B_t(.) are closed, B^o_t(.) open; integral^- denotes the lower Lebesgue integral (lintegral).

1. Elementary facts.
 (a) graphPoint is linear: graphPoint x y - graphPoint x' y' = graphPoint (x - x') (y - y'), and ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2. Indeed the coordinates of graphPoint x y are those of x followed by those of y (Fin.append), and the squared Euclidean norm is the sum of squared coordinates; split the sum over Fin (n + l) into the first n and the last l indices (Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right).
 (b) For x, x' in B^n_R(0): ||F(x) - F(x')|| = ||graphPoint (x - x') (f x - f x')|| (q is a linear isometry and (a)) = (||x - x'||^2 + ||f x - f x'||^2)^(1/2) <= sqrt(2) ||x - x'||, because f is 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) (iii).
 (c) F(0) = q(graphPoint 0 0) = 0 by (ii), so (b) with x' = 0 gives ||F(x)|| <= sqrt(2) ||x|| for x in B^n_R(0).
 (d) For every continuous linear T of R^(n+l): hsNormSq(T) = sum_i ||T e_i||^2 <= (n + l) ||T||^2, since ||T e_i|| <= ||T|| ||e_i|| = ||T||. Every orthogonal projection P_W = W.starProjection has ||P_W|| <= 1 (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le), and by its definition V.tangentProj w is either such a projection or 0, so ||p_w|| <= 1 for every w. Hence for every subspace Q: 0 <= hsNormSq(p_w - Q.starProjection) <= (n + l)(||p_w|| + ||Q.starProjection||)^2 <= 4(n + l).
 (e) T -> hsNormSq(T - P) is continuous for each fixed P (finite sum of squared norms of the continuous evaluations T -> (T - P) e_i).

2. Fix z in B^n_{R/4}(0) and 0 < s <= R/4. Put zeta := F(z), Q := S(zeta), P := Q.starProjection, D := B^n_{s/2}(z) (a closed, hence measurable, subset of R^n) and B := B_s(zeta) (closed ball of R^(n+l)).
 (a) zeta lies in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0): by 1(c), ||zeta|| <= sqrt(2) ||z|| <= sqrt(2) R/4 < R/2 <= R. Since ||z|| <= R/4 <= R, zeta = q(graphPoint z (f z)) belongs to q(graphOver f (B^n_R(0))), and also to B_R(0); by (iv), zeta is in spt V cap B_R(0), so zeta is in spt V, and with ||zeta|| <= R/2 we get zeta in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0).
 (b) D is contained in B^o_{R/2}(0): for x in D, ||x|| <= ||z|| + s/2 <= R/4 + R/8 = 3R/8 < R/2. In particular D is contained in B^n_R(0).
 (c) B is contained in B_R(0), hence in U by (i): for y in B, ||y|| <= ||zeta|| + s <= sqrt(2) R/4 + R/4 < R. B is compact (closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional space).

3. mu(B) < infinity. By definition mu = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity(ofReal o theta). Since B is measurable, mu(B) = integral^-_B ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) = integral^-_{M cap B} ofReal(theta) dH^n (withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict). By the structure field integrableOn_mult applied to the compact set B contained in U (step 2(c)), theta is H^n-integrable on M cap B, so integral^-_{M cap B} ofReal(theta) dH^n <= integral^-_{M cap B} ||theta||_e dH^n < infinity.

4. Integrability and Bochner form. Let h(y) := hsNormSq(p_y - P). By (v) and 1(e), h is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous function of an a.e. strongly measurable map), and 0 <= h <= 4(n + l) by 1(d). As mu(B) < infinity (step 3), h is mu-integrable on B (a bounded a.e. strongly measurable function on a finite-measure set: Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with mu(B) != infinity, or Integrable.of_bound for the finite measure mu restricted to B). Hence (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) integral^-_B ofReal(h) dmu = ofReal(integral_B h dmu).

5. Tilt bound. By definition, V.tiltExcess zeta s Q = (s^n)^(-1) integral_B h dmu, and s^n > 0, so integral_B h dmu = s^n V.tiltExcess zeta s Q. By step 2(a) and 0 < s <= R/4 <= R/2, hypothesis (vii) gives V.tiltExcess zeta s Q <= A (s/R)^e; multiplying by s^n > 0: integral_B h dmu <= A s^n (s/R)^e. With step 4: integral^-_B ofReal(h) dmu <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^e).

6. Comparison. Define Phi(w, T) := indicator_B(w) * ofReal(hsNormSq(T - P)) (value in [0, infinity]). It is jointly measurable: (w, T) -> indicator_B(w) is measurable (B closed, composition with the measurable first projection), (w, T) -> ofReal(hsNormSq(T - P)) is measurable (continuous function of the measurable second projection, 1(e)), and products of measurable [0, infinity]-valued functions are measurable. D is measurable and contained in B^o_{R/2}(0) (step 2(b)), so hypothesis (vi) gives
 integral^-_D Phi(F(x), G(x)) dx <= integral^-_{q(graphOver f D)} Phi(y, p_y) dmu(y).
 (a) Left side. For x in D, x and z lie in B^n_R(0), so by 1(b) ||F(x) - zeta|| <= sqrt(2) ||x - z|| <= sqrt(2) s/2 < s; thus F(x) is in B and Phi(F(x), G(x)) = ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - P)). As D is measurable, the left side equals integral^-_D ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - P)) dx (setLIntegral_congr_fun).
 (b) Right side. Restricting the measure to the set q(graphOver f D) can only decrease the lower integral of a nonnegative function (setLIntegral_le_lintegral), and integral^- indicator_B(y) ofReal(h(y)) dmu(y) = integral^-_B ofReal(h) dmu (lintegral_indicator, B measurable). So the right side is <= integral^-_B ofReal(h) dmu.

7. Conclusion. Combining steps 6 and 5:
 integral^-_{B^n_{s/2}(z)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - (S(F(z))).starProjection)) dx <= integral^-_B ofReal(h) dmu <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^e).
 Since z in B^n_{R/4}(0) and s in (0, R/4] were arbitrary, the theorem follows.
proof_key_steps: Graph geometry: |F(x) - F(x')| <= sqrt(2)|x - x'| on B^n_R(0), |F(x)| <= sqrt(2)|x|, and 0 <= hsNormSq(p_w - P) <= 4(n+l) via operator norms of projections
zeta = F(z) lies in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0); D = B^n_{s/2}(z) lies in B^o_{R/2}(0); B_s(zeta) is a compact subset of B_R(0), hence of U
mu(B_s(zeta)) < infinity from integrableOn_mult; the bounded a.e. strongly measurable integrand is integrable, so its lintegral is ofReal(s^n E(zeta, s, S zeta)) <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^e)
Apply the comparison hypothesis to Phi(w, T) = 1_{B_s(zeta)}(w) ofReal(hsNormSq(T - P)): the indicator is 1 along F(D) and the right side is at most the lintegral over B_s(zeta)

subproblems.title: Lebesgue points identify the Campanato centres almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, m, k >= 0, G, c : R^n -> L(R^m, R^k) (continuous linear maps with the operator norm ||.||) and A, R, alpha, B real with R > 0 and alpha > 0. Assume G is Borel measurable, ||G(x)|| <= B for every x, and for every z in the closed ball B_{R/4}(0) and every 0 < s <= R/4: lintegral over the closed ball B_{s/2}(z) of ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z))) dx <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)), where hsNormSq(T) = sum_i ||T e_i||^2. Then G(z) = c(z) for Lebesgue-almost every z in the open ball B^o_{R/4}(0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n m k : ℕ) (G c : Rn n → (Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k)) (A R α B : ℝ), 1 ≤ n → 0 < R → 0 < α → Measurable G → (∀ x, ‖G x‖ ≤ B) → (∀ z ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) (R / 4), ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ R / 4 → ∫⁻ x in closedBall z (s / 2), ENNReal.ofReal (hsNormSq (G x - c z)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (A * s ^ n * (s / R) ^ (2 * α))) → ∀ᵐ z ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), z ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (R / 4) → G z = c z
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (identification almost everywhere by Lebesgue's differentiation theorem in the parameter domain R^n), stated for an abstract measurable bounded G and arbitrary centres c.

Notation. L = L(R^m, R^k) with the operator norm ||.||; hsNormSq(T) := sum_{i<m} ||T e_i||^2 (e_i the standard basis of R^m); balls B_t(z) are closed, B^o_t(z) open; L^n is Lebesgue measure (volume) on R^n; integral^- is the lower Lebesgue integral (lintegral). (Camp) denotes the hypothesis: for every z in B_{R/4}(0) and 0 < s <= R/4, integral^-_{B_{s/2}(z)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z))) dx <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)).

1. Hilbert-Schmidt facts. For T, T' in L:
 (a) hsNormSq(T) >= 0, and hsNormSq(T) = 0 implies T e_i = 0 for every i, hence T = 0 (a linear map vanishing on a basis is zero).
 (b) hsNormSq(T) <= m ||T||^2, because ||T e_i|| <= ||T|| ||e_i|| = ||T||.
 (c) hsNormSq(T - T') <= 2 hsNormSq(T) + 2 hsNormSq(T'), summing ||a - b||^2 <= 2||a||^2 + 2||b||^2 over a = T e_i, b = T' e_i.
 (d) T -> hsNormSq(T - T0) is continuous for fixed T0, so x -> hsNormSq(G(x) - T0) is measurable (G is measurable).

2. Balls. v := L^n(B_1(0)) is positive and finite (Lebesgue measure is an additive Haar measure: closed balls of positive radius have positive measure and are compact), and L^n(B_t(z)) = t^n v for every z and t >= 0 (Measure.addHaar_closedBall' with finrank R^n = n).

3. Lebesgue points. Since R^n is nonempty, B >= ||G(0)|| >= 0. G is measurable (hence a.e. strongly measurable, L being finite dimensional) and bounded by B, so it is integrable on every compact set, i.e. locally integrable. By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for the doubling measure L^n (IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, with K = 1, index filter t -> 0+, centres w(t) = z and radii delta(t) = t; z lies in B_{1*t}(z)), there is an L^n-null set N such that for every z not in N:
 a(z, t) := (t^n v)^(-1) integral_{B_t(z)} ||G(x) - G(z)|| dx -> 0 as t -> 0+.

4. Key inequality. Let z be in B^o_{R/4}(0) and not in N, let 0 < s <= R/4 and t := s/2. Then z is in B_{R/4}(0), so (Camp) applies at z. For every x, apply 1(c) to T := G(x) - c(z) and T' := G(x) - G(z) (so T - T' = G(z) - c(z)), then 1(b) and ||G(x) - G(z)|| <= 2B:
 hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z)) <= 2 hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z)) + 2 m ||G(x) - G(z)||^2 <= 2 hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z)) + 4 m B ||G(x) - G(z)||.
 Apply ofReal (monotone, additive on nonnegative reals) and integrate over B_t(z) with respect to L^n; the integrands are measurable (1(d)), so the lower integral is additive:
 ofReal(hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z))) * L^n(B_t(z)) <= 2 integral^-_{B_t(z)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z))) dx + ofReal(4 m B) integral^-_{B_t(z)} ofReal(||G(x) - G(z)||) dx.
 By (Camp) the first term is <= 2 ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)). The function x -> ||G(x) - G(z)|| is bounded by 2B and measurable, hence integrable on the finite-measure ball, so its lower integral is ofReal of its Bochner integral, which equals t^n v a(z, t). Since L^n(B_t(z)) = t^n v = 2^(-n) s^n v is positive and finite, dividing (and passing to real numbers) gives, with A+ := max(A, 0):
 hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z)) <= 2^(n+1) v^(-1) A+ (s/R)^(2 alpha) + 4 m B a(z, s/2).

5. Limit. Let s -> 0+. Since alpha > 0 and R > 0, (s/R)^(2 alpha) -> 0; by step 3, a(z, s/2) -> 0. Hence hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z)) <= 0, so hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z)) = 0 and G(z) = c(z) by 1(a).

6. Conclusion. Every z in B^o_{R/4}(0) with G(z) != c(z) lies in the null set N. Hence for L^n-a.e. z: z in B^o_{R/4}(0) implies G(z) = c(z).
proof_key_steps: Hilbert-Schmidt facts: hsNormSq(T - T') <= 2 hsNormSq(T) + 2 hsNormSq(T'), hsNormSq(T) <= m ||T||^2, hsNormSq(T) = 0 only for T = 0
Measurable bounded G is locally integrable; Lebesgue differentiation gives a null set off which the ball averages of ||G - G(z)|| tend to 0
Averaging the pointwise inequality over B_{s/2}(z): hsNormSq(G(z) - c(z)) <= 2^(n+1) v^-1 max(A,0) (s/R)^(2 alpha) + 4 m B a(z, s/2)
Letting s -> 0+ forces G(z) = c(z) off the null set

subproblems.title: Campanato centres are Hoelder continuous (midpoint averaging)
subproblems.statement: For every n >= 1 there is C >= 0, depending only on n, such that: for all m, k >= 0, all G, c : R^n -> L(R^m, R^k), A >= 0, R > 0 and 0 < alpha <= 1 with G Borel measurable and lintegral over the closed ball B_{s/2}(z) of ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z))) dx <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)) for every z in the closed ball B_{R/4}(0) and every 0 < s <= R/4, one has hsNorm(c(x) - c(y)) <= C sqrt(A) (||x - y||/R)^alpha for all x, y in the open ball B^o_{R/16}(0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (m k : ℕ) (G c : Rn n → (Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k)) (A R α : ℝ), 0 ≤ A → 0 < R → 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → Measurable G → (∀ z ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) (R / 4), ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ R / 4 → ∫⁻ x in closedBall z (s / 2), ENNReal.ofReal (hsNormSq (G x - c z)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (A * s ^ n * (s / R) ^ (2 * α))) → ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (R / 16), ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (R / 16), hsNorm (c x - c y) ≤ C * Real.sqrt A * (‖x - y‖ / R) ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (the Hoelder argument after book (11): midpoint averaging of two Campanato bounds). The parent's computation never uses that x_1, x_2 are Lebesgue points, so it is stated here for all pairs in B^o_{R/16}(0). The constant uses v_n := L^n(B_1(0)), which equals omega_n; its explicit Gamma-function value is not needed.

Notation. hsNormSq(T) := sum_{i<m} ||T e_i||^2, hsNorm := sqrt(hsNormSq); balls B_t(.) are closed, B^o_t(.) open; L^n is Lebesgue measure on R^n and integral^- the lower Lebesgue integral. (Camp): for every z in B_{R/4}(0) and 0 < s <= R/4, integral^-_{B_{s/2}(z)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(x) - c(z))) dx <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)).

1. Constant. v_n := L^n(B_1(0)) is positive and finite, and L^n(B_t(w)) = t^n v_n for all w and t >= 0 (Measure.addHaar_closedBall', finrank R^n = n). Put C := (2^(2n+4)/v_n)^(1/2) >= 0. C depends only on n.

2. Hilbert-Schmidt facts. hsNormSq(T) >= 0 and hsNormSq(0) = 0; hsNormSq(T - T') <= 2 hsNormSq(T) + 2 hsNormSq(T') (sum ||a - b||^2 <= 2||a||^2 + 2||b||^2 over a = T e_i, b = T' e_i); T -> hsNormSq(T - T0) is continuous, so x -> hsNormSq(G(x) - T0) is measurable for fixed T0.

Now let m, k, G, c, A >= 0, R > 0, 0 < alpha <= 1 with G measurable and (Camp), and let x, y be in B^o_{R/16}(0).

3. The case x = y. Then hsNorm(c(x) - c(y)) = hsNorm(0) = 0, and C sqrt(A) (0/R)^alpha = 0 because alpha > 0. The inequality holds.

4. Geometry for x != y. Put d := ||x - y||, so 0 < d <= ||x|| + ||y|| < R/8, s := 2d (so 0 < s < R/4 and s/2 = d), m0 := (x + y)/2 and B' := B_{d/2}(m0). For w in B', ||w - x|| <= ||w - m0|| + ||m0 - x|| <= d/2 + d/2 = d, and likewise ||w - y|| <= d; so B' is contained in B_d(x) cap B_d(y) = B_{s/2}(x) cap B_{s/2}(y). Also x, y lie in B_{R/4}(0), so (Camp) applies at z = x and z = y with this s.

5. Pointwise bound. For every w, c(x) - c(y) = (G(w) - c(y)) - (G(w) - c(x)), so by step 2
 hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y)) <= 2 hsNormSq(G(w) - c(x)) + 2 hsNormSq(G(w) - c(y)).

6. Averaging. Apply ofReal and integrate over B' (lower integral; the two integrands on the right are measurable, so the lower integral is additive; the integral of a constant over B' is the constant times L^n(B')), then enlarge the domains (monotonicity of the lower integral in the set) and use (Camp) at x and at y:
 ofReal(hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y))) L^n(B') <= 2 integral^-_{B'} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(w) - c(x))) dw + 2 integral^-_{B'} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(w) - c(y))) dw
 <= 2 integral^-_{B_{s/2}(x)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(w) - c(x))) dw + 2 integral^-_{B_{s/2}(y)} ofReal(hsNormSq(G(w) - c(y))) dw
 <= 4 ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha)).

7. Arithmetic. L^n(B') = (d/2)^n v_n is positive and finite; dividing and passing to real numbers (A >= 0):
 hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y)) <= 4 A (2d)^n (2d/R)^(2 alpha) / ((d/2)^n v_n).
 Now (2d)^n/(d/2)^n = 4^n, and (2d/R)^(2 alpha) = 2^(2 alpha) (d/R)^(2 alpha) (Real.mul_rpow with nonnegative factors), and 2^(2 alpha) <= 2^2 = 4 because 0 < 2 alpha <= 2 and the base 2 is >= 1. Hence
 hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y)) <= 4^(n+2) A (d/R)^(2 alpha) / v_n = C^2 A ((d/R)^alpha)^2,
 using 4^(n+2) = 2^(2n+4) and (d/R)^(2 alpha) = ((d/R)^alpha)^2 (d/R >= 0, Real.rpow_mul / rpow_natCast).

8. Square roots. All factors are nonnegative, so taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, sqrt of a product of nonnegative numbers, sqrt(u^2) = u for u >= 0):
 hsNorm(c(x) - c(y)) = sqrt(hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y))) <= C sqrt(A) (||x - y||/R)^alpha.
 Together with step 3 this proves the claim for all x, y in B^o_{R/16}(0), with C depending only on n.
proof_key_steps: C := (2^(2n+4)/v_n)^(1/2), v_n the Lebesgue measure of the closed unit ball, L^n(B_t(w)) = t^n v_n
For x != y with d = |x - y| < R/8, the ball B_{d/2}((x+y)/2) lies in B_d(x) cap B_d(y)
Pointwise hsNormSq(c(x) - c(y)) <= 2 hsNormSq(G - c(x)) + 2 hsNormSq(G - c(y)); average over the midpoint ball and use the Campanato bound with s = 2d at x and at y
Arithmetic 4 * 4^n * 2^(2 alpha) <= 2^(2n+4) and square roots give hsNorm(c(x) - c(y)) <= C sqrt(A)(d/R)^alpha

subproblems.title: A Lipschitz map whose a.e. derivative is continuous has that derivative everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l, g : R^n -> L(R^n, R^l), c in R^n, r real and K >= 0. If f is K-Lipschitz on the open ball B^o_r(c), g is continuous on B^o_r(c), and for Lebesgue-almost every x in B^o_r(c) the map f has Frechet derivative g(x) at x, then f has Frechet derivative g(x) at every x in B^o_r(c).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (g : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith K f (ball c r) → ContinuousOn g (ball c r) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ ball c r → HasFDerivAt f (g x) x) → ∀ x ∈ ball c r, HasFDerivAt f (g x) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the analytic core of step 5 of the parent proof ('f is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous along segments; for a.e. y the segment y + [0,1]h meets the bad set in a null set (Fubini); f(y + h) - f(y) = integral_0^1 g(y + th)h dt; both sides are continuous in y; hence f is differentiable everywhere with derivative g'), stated for an arbitrary continuous a.e.-derivative g.

Notation. B := B^o_r(c) (open ball; if r <= 0 then B is empty and there is nothing to prove). L = L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. L^n, L^1 are Lebesgue measures on R^n and R. Closed balls B_t(.).

0. Preliminaries. B is open and convex, f is continuous on B (Lipschitz). Let N0 := {x in B : f does not have Frechet derivative g(x) at x}; by hypothesis L^n(N0) = 0. Choose a Borel set N containing N0 with L^n(N) = 0 (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Then f has derivative g(p) at every p in B minus N.

1. Fubini: almost every parallel segment meets N in a null set. Fix x, y in B and put h := y - x. The map Psi(w, t) := x + w + t h from R^n x R to R^n is continuous (so measurable for the product sigma-algebra), hence E := Psi^(-1)(N) is measurable. For each t in R, {w : (w, t) in E} = {w : w + (x + t h) in N} is a translate of N, so it has L^n-measure L^n(N) = 0 (translation invariance of Lebesgue measure). By Tonelli (Measure.prod_apply_symm), (L^n x L^1)(E) = integral^- L^n({w : (w, t) in E}) dt = 0. By Measure.measure_prod_null, for L^n-a.e. w: L^1({t in R : x + w + t h in N}) = 0. Call such w good.

2. FTC along a good segment. Since B is open, choose rho > 0 with B^o_rho(x) and B^o_rho(y) contained in B. Fix a good w with ||w|| < rho. For t in [0, 1] put sigma(t) := x + w + t h = (1 - t)(x + w) + t(y + w); since x + w is in B^o_rho(x), y + w is in B^o_rho(y) and B is convex, sigma(t) is in B. The set {t : sigma(t) in B} is open and contains [0, 1]. Define k(t) := g(sigma(t)) h in R^l, Gamma(t) := f(sigma(t)), Psi1(t) := integral_0^t k(tau) dtau and phi := Gamma - Psi1.
 (a) g is continuous on the open set B, hence continuous at every point of B; therefore k is continuous at every t with sigma(t) in B, in particular on [0, 1], and k is bounded on [0, 1] by some K1 (compactness).
 (b) phi is Lipschitz on [0, 1]: ||Gamma(t) - Gamma(t')|| <= K ||sigma(t) - sigma(t')|| = K ||h|| |t - t'| (both points in B), and ||Psi1(t) - Psi1(t')|| = ||integral_{t'}^t k|| <= K1 |t - t'|. Hence phi is absolutely continuous on [0, 1] (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval).
 (c) phi'(t) = 0 for a.e. t in [0, 1]: because w is good, for all t outside an L^1-null set, sigma(t) is not in N; take such t in the open interval (0, 1) (the endpoints form a null set). Then sigma(t) is in B minus N, so f has derivative g(sigma(t)) at sigma(t), and by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt, sigma has derivative h) Gamma has derivative g(sigma(t)) h = k(t) at t. Also k is interval integrable on [0, t], strongly measurable near t (continuous on a neighbourhood of t) and continuous at t, so by the first fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right) Psi1 has derivative k(t) at t. Hence phi has derivative 0 at t.
 (d) By AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.const_of_ae_hasDerivAt_zero (valid for R^l-valued maps), phi is constant on [0, 1]; phi(1) = phi(0) gives
 f(y + w) - f(x + w) = Gamma(1) - Gamma(0) = Psi1(1) = integral_0^1 g(x + w + tau h) h dtau.

3. Removing w. The good w with ||w|| < rho form a subset of B^o_rho(0) of full measure, hence a dense subset of B^o_rho(0) (each nonempty open subset of B^o_rho(0) has positive Lebesgue measure). Choose good w_j with ||w_j|| < rho/2 and w_j -> 0. Then:
 (a) f(y + w_j) - f(x + w_j) -> f(y) - f(x), since f is continuous on B and y + w_j -> y, x + w_j -> x inside B.
 (b) Let K_rho := {(1 - tau) a + tau b : a in B_{rho/2}(x), b in B_{rho/2}(y), tau in [0, 1]}. It is compact (continuous image of a product of compact sets) and contained in B (B_{rho/2}(x) is contained in B^o_rho(x), B_{rho/2}(y) in B^o_rho(y), and B is convex). For ||w|| <= rho/2 and tau in [0, 1], x + w + tau h = (1 - tau)(x + w) + tau(y + w) is in K_rho. g is continuous on the compact set K_rho, hence bounded there by some K2 and uniformly continuous there. Therefore g(x + w_j + tau h) h -> g(x + tau h) h uniformly in tau in [0, 1] (alternatively: dominated convergence with the constant bound K2 ||h||), so integral_0^1 g(x + w_j + tau h) h dtau -> integral_0^1 g(x + tau h) h dtau.
 Passing to the limit in 2(d) (applied to w = w_j):
 (FTC) f(y) - f(x) = integral_0^1 g(x + tau (y - x)) (y - x) dtau for all x, y in B.

4. Differentiability. Fix x in B and epsilon > 0. Choose eta > 0 with B^o_eta(x) contained in B and ||g(z) - g(x)|| <= epsilon for all z in B^o_eta(x) (g is continuous at x). Let ||h|| < eta. Then x + tau h is in B^o_eta(x) for tau in [0, 1], and by (FTC) with y = x + h,
 f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h = integral_0^1 (g(x + tau h) - g(x)) h dtau,
 whose norm is <= epsilon ||h||. Hence ||f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h|| <= epsilon ||h|| for all sufficiently small h, for every epsilon > 0; that is, f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h = o(||h||) as h -> 0 (hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero, Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff). So f has Frechet derivative g(x) at x, for every x in B.
proof_key_steps: Enclose the bad points in a Borel null set N
Tonelli plus translation invariance: for a.e. w the segment x + w + [0,1](y - x) meets N in an L^1-null set
On such a segment f(sigma(t)) - integral_0^t g(sigma) h is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous, with a.e. zero derivative, hence constant
Let w -> 0 through good w (dense), using continuity of f and uniform continuity of g on a compact convex subset: f(y) - f(x) = integral_0^1 g(x + t(y - x))(y - x) dt
Continuity of g at x gives f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x)h = o(|h|)

subproblems.title: A Lipschitz map with Hoelder derivative on a full-measure set is C^1 with the same Hoelder bound
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l, c in R^n, r real, K >= 0, Z a subset of R^n, and M, R, alpha real with M >= 0, R > 0 and alpha > 0. Assume f is K-Lipschitz on the open ball B := B^o_r(c), Z is contained in B, B minus Z is Lebesgue-null, f is differentiable at every point of Z, and hsNorm(Df(x) - Df(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha for all x, y in Z, where Df = fderiv f and hsNorm is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Then f is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn R 1 f B) and hsNorm(Df(x) - Df(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha for all x, y in B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (Z : Set (Rn n)) (M R α : ℝ), 0 ≤ M → 0 < R → 0 < α → LipschitzOnWith K f (ball c r) → Z ⊆ ball c r → volume (ball c r \ Z) = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ Z, ∀ y ∈ Z, hsNorm (fderiv ℝ f x - fderiv ℝ f y) ≤ M * (‖x - y‖ / R) ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball c r) ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball c r, ∀ y ∈ ball c r, hsNorm (fderiv ℝ f x - fderiv ℝ f y) ≤ M * (‖x - y‖ / R) ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ('By (H), Df restricted to Z is uniformly continuous, and Z is dense (full measure); let g be the unique continuous map with g = Df on Z; g satisfies (H) on the whole ball; ... f is differentiable at every point with fderiv f = g, which is continuous; so f is C^1 and (H) holds on the whole ball'), for an arbitrary Hoelder modulus M (t/R)^alpha. The everywhere-differentiability is the sibling theorem allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae.

Notation. B := B^o_r(c) (open ball; if r <= 0, B is empty and both conclusions are trivial). L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm ||.||; it is finite dimensional, hence complete. hsNorm(T) := (sum_{i<n} ||T e_i||^2)^(1/2). kappa(t) := M (t/R)^alpha for t >= 0; since M >= 0, R > 0 and alpha > 0, kappa is continuous and nondecreasing on [0, infinity) with kappa(0) = 0. Df(x) := fderiv f x.

1. Hilbert-Schmidt versus operator norm. For T in L and v in R^n, write v = sum_i v_i e_i with ||v||^2 = sum_i v_i^2. Then ||T v|| <= sum_i |v_i| ||T e_i|| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i ||T e_i||^2)^(1/2) = ||v|| hsNorm(T) (Cauchy-Schwarz for finite sums). Hence ||T|| <= hsNorm(T) (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). Moreover hsNorm is continuous on L (square root of a finite sum of squared norms of the continuous evaluations T -> T e_i).

2. Density. Z is dense in B: let x be in B and epsilon > 0; W := B^o_epsilon(x) cap B is open and nonempty (it contains x), so L^n(W) > 0. If W did not meet Z, W would be contained in B minus Z, which has measure 0; contradiction. Hence B is contained in the closure of Z, and for every x in B the filter of neighbourhoods of x within Z (nhdsWithin x Z) is nontrivial.

3. Limits along Z. Let x be in B. For eta > 0 and z, z' in Z cap B^o_eta(x): ||Df(z) - Df(z')|| <= hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) <= kappa(||z - z'||) <= kappa(2 eta) (step 1, hypothesis, monotonicity of kappa). Since kappa(2 eta) -> 0 as eta -> 0+, the image of nhdsWithin x Z under Df is a Cauchy filter on the complete space L, hence converges. Define g := extendFrom Z Df (the limit of Df along nhdsWithin x Z). Then for every x in B, Df(z) -> g(x) as z -> x within Z (extendFrom_eq), and g is continuous on B (continuousOn_extendFrom, using step 2). If x is in Z, then ||Df(z) - Df(x)|| <= kappa(||z - x||) -> 0 as z -> x, so g(x) = Df(x) (limits in the Hausdorff space L are unique).

4. Hoelder bound for g. Let x, y be in B. Along the nontrivial product filter (nhdsWithin x Z) x (nhdsWithin y Z): Df(z) - Df(z') -> g(x) - g(y), hence hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) -> hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) (step 1, continuity of hsNorm); and kappa(||z - z'||) -> kappa(||x - y||) (continuity of the norm and of kappa). Since z, z' are eventually in Z, the hypothesis gives hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) <= kappa(||z - z'||) eventually, and passing to the limit (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto): hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) <= kappa(||x - y||).

5. Differentiability everywhere. For x in Z, f is differentiable at x, so f has Frechet derivative Df(x) = g(x) at x (step 3). Hence the set of x in B at which f does not have derivative g(x) is contained in B minus Z, which is L^n-null; that is, for L^n-a.e. x: x in B implies HasFDerivAt f (g x) x. Since f is K-Lipschitz on B and g is continuous on B (step 3), the sibling theorem allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae (with this f, g, c, r, K) gives HasFDerivAt f (g x) x for every x in B. Consequently f is differentiable on B and fderiv f x = g(x) for every x in B.

6. C^1. B is open, f is differentiable on B, and fderiv f coincides on B with g, which is continuous on B (step 3); so fderiv f is continuous on B (ContinuousOn.congr). By contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen with order 0 + 1 = 1, f is C^1 on B: ContDiffOn R 1 f B. (In this Mathlib the right side of that equivalence consists of DifferentiableOn f B, the clause (0 = ω → AnalyticOn f B), where ω is the analytic smoothness order and the clause holds trivially since 0 ≠ ω, and ContDiffOn 0 (fderiv f) B, which is continuity of fderiv f on B by contDiffOn_zero.)

7. Hoelder bound for Df. For x, y in B, by steps 5 and 4: hsNorm(fderiv f x - fderiv f y) = hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha.
proof_key_steps: ||T|| <= hsNorm(T) (Cauchy-Schwarz) and continuity of hsNorm
Z is dense in B since B minus Z is null and nonempty open sets have positive measure
The Hoelder bound makes Df Cauchy along Z, so g := extendFrom Z Df is continuous on B and equals Df on Z
Passing to the limit along Z x Z gives the Hoelder bound for g on all of B
Sibling allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae gives fderiv f = g on B, hence C^1 (contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen) and the Hoelder bound
